end.summary:
Vihaan described the court structure as District Court → High Court → Supreme Court and explained appeal.
They identified civil and criminal case examples, with some uncertainty about a traffic accident.
They explored judicial review and said courts can check laws against constitutional rights and stop unconstitutional laws.
They initially questioned judicial independence and later stated judges cannot be removed simply because the Prime Minister is unhappy.
They asked about free legal aid and how people without money can access courts; teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Asha practised the court hierarchy, appeals, civil and criminal cases, judicial review, judicial independence, and access to justice. Vihaan used the court sequence and appeal method correctly, and later corrected the idea that a judge must follow the government because it pays their salary. The mix-up about whether government pressure can remove or control a judge was only partly addressed by the end. At home, ask them to explain three routes to justice—free legal aid, Lok Adalat, and PIL—and give one example for each.

Toh court... hmm... agar kaanoon Samvidhaan ke khilaaf hai toh... court usse cancel kar sakta hai na? Null... pata nahi shabd. Par haan, woh kaanoon nahi chalega. Galat toh nahi bol raha?

Aap keh rahe hain ki Samvidhaan ke khilaaf kaanoon nahi chalega; haan, court use radd kar sakta hai. Isse kaanoon ko strike down karna kehte hain. Ab judges ke faislon ki azaadi par sochiye: agar koi kahe ki sarkaar tankhwah deti hai, isliye judges ko Prime Minister ki baat maanni padti hai, toh us baat mein kya galat hai?

Arre... pata nahi. Matlab tankhwah sarkaar deti hai, toh judge ko sunna padega na? Woh log independent kaise honge phir? Mujhse nahi hoga, yeh sab complicated hai. Whiteboard pe woh line dikhao na, 'Khilaaf? → court ka' ka matlab kya hai?

Yeh complicated lag raha hai, toh ek chhota example lete hain. Football referee ko payment milti hai, par faisla rules se hota hai, paise dene wale ki marzi se nahi; judge bhi kanoon aur Samvidhaan ke hisaab se faisla karta hai, aur sarkaar sirf faisla na pasand hone par use hata nahi sakti. Whiteboard ki adhoori line ka matlab hai: agar kanoon Samvidhaan ke khilaaf ho, court use radd kar sakta hai. Judge faisla kis ke hisaab se karega: Prime Minister ki marzi se ya kanoon aur Samvidhaan se?
Judge faisla kanoon aur Samvidhaan ke hisaab se karega... par agar tankhwah sarkaar deti hai toh Prime Minister ko mana karne se darr nahi lagega kya?

Haan, darr ka sawaal bilkul samajh aata hai. Judge ki tankhwah sarkaari funds se aati hai, par Prime Minister unhe sirf apna faisla na maanne par naukri se nahi hata sakte; judge ko kanoon aur Samvidhaan ke hisaab se faisla karna hota hai. Ab agar Prime Minister ko judge ka faisla pasand na aaye, kya woh sirf is wajah se judge ko hata sakte hain?
nahi... nahi hata sakte, woh bhi independent hote hain. Par... par phir bhi, agar PM naraz ho toh press mein unki burai toh karwa sakta hai na?

Haan, sirf faisla pasand na aane par PM judge ko hata nahi sakte. Press mein kisi faisle ki aalochana ho sakti hai, aur judge par dabav bhi mehsoos ho sakta hai; lekin isse PM ko judge ko hukm dene ka adhikaar nahi milta. Isliye judge ki azaadi ko bachana zaroori hai. Ab agar kisi ke paas lawyer ke paise na hon, kya uske liye court ka raasta band ho jaata hai?
Haan... agar paise nahi hain toh court kaise jaayenge, pata nahi. Garib logo ke liye toh court nahi hai, lawyer fees bohot hoti hai. Photo dikhao na, free legal aid jaisa kuch hota hai?

Haan, lawyer ki fees rukawat ban sakti hai, par gareeb logon ke liye bhi court ka raasta hai. Abhi photo nahi bana sakti; shabdon mein sochiye: court ke paas ek madad desk hai, jahaan zarooratmand log muft kanooni madad, yaani free legal aid, ke baare mein pooch sakte hain. Toh paise na hon, tab bhi kanooni madad mil sakti hai na?

c8-sst-ch11-t01-s3.evidence: Judge ki independence aur PM ke na hata sakne ki baat kahi; press ke dabav ko lekar sawaal hai, card ka verified grade nahi mila.
